itens.readme:
# UI SDK
A library of behaviors for agents to build the next generation of user interfaces.
Keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop and the ARIA they need live in `@ui-sdk/core`, with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components.
**[Read the docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs)**
## Install
UI SDK is in beta. Install core and the adapter for your framework:
```bash
npm install @ui-sdk/react @ui-sdk/core
```
For other frameworks, swap `@ui-sdk/react` for `@ui-sdk/vue`, `@ui-sdk/svelte`, `@ui-sdk/solid` or `@ui-sdk/web`.
Then give your agent the UI SDK skill:
```bash
npx skills@latest add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk
```
## Example
Every component in UI SDK is built from behaviors. You start by creating the primitive with behaviors.
Don't worry, you don't need to learn how to write this. Your agents will. And we made them really good at it.
```ts
import { createFocusRecovery, definePrimitive } from "@ui-sdk/core"
const searchField = definePrimitive({
  name: "search-field",
  state: () => ({ value: "" }),
  api: (context) => ({
    set: (value: string) => context.store.set({ value }),
    recovery: createFocusRecovery({ fallback: () => context.element("input") }),
  }),
  slots: (slot) => ({
    input: slot({
      attrs: (state) => ({ value: state.value }),
      on: {
        input: (event, { api }) =>
          api.set((event.target as HTMLInputElement).value),
      },
    }),
    clear: slot({
      present: (state) => state.value !== "",
      attrs: () => ({ type: "button" }),
      press: ({ api }) => api.set(""),
      bind: (el, part) => part.api.recovery.bind(el, part),
    }),
  }),
})
export { searchField }
```
Then render it in your framework with `createParts`. The parts are the same in all five.

```tsx
import { createParts } from "@ui-sdk/react/primitive"
import { searchField } from "./search-field"
const parts = createParts(searchField, { input: "input", clear: "button" })
const SearchField = parts.Root
const SearchFieldInput = parts.Input
const SearchFieldClear = parts.Clear
```

 OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative: an independent project inspired by **Grok Bot**, and the open-source alternative to **Meta Muse**, **OpenAI dots** and **Cue by Manus** — bring-your-own-agent, local-first, on the models you already have. itens.descricao_en: Best headless browser for AI agents. Lite, Fast, High-Compatibility. Built in Rust
itens.readme:
Moli 
   English  |
   简体中文  |
   日本語  |
   Deutsch  |
   Français  |
   Español  |
   한국어 
Moli is a production-ready headless browser for AI agents. Its on-demand layout
and rendering design combines a complete browser runtime with a lightweight
resource footprint.
Moli helps your AI agent fetch and extract web pages, search the web, and
automate browser tasks.
Use it through the CLI, CDP, WebDriver Classic, or WebDriver BiDi.
Moli supports Linux, macOS, and Windows.
## Quick start
Give this prompt to your AI agent:
```text
Install the skills under https://github.com/lexmount/moli/tree/main/skills,
follow their instructions to download and install the latest prebuilt Moli
binary, then use moli-webfetch to fetch https://example.com and show me the
result.
```
### Direct installation
On Linux or macOS:
```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL \
  https://github.com/lexmount/moli/releases/latest/download/moli-installer.sh | sh
```
On Windows, run in PowerShell:
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://github.com/lexmount/moli/releases/latest/download/moli-installer.ps1 | iex"
```
## Showcase
   An HTML5 game rendered by Moli and inspected live through Chrome DevTools. 
   rust-lang.org rendered by Moli, with its live DOM, CSS, and geometry available in Chrome DevTools. 
## CLI usage
### Extract a page
Render the page as Markdown with Moli's default completion strategy:
```bash
moli fetch \
  --dump markdown \
  --wait done \
  https://example.com
```
Or directly return a compact, model-friendly semantic tree:
```bash
moli fetch \
  --dump semantic_tree_text \
  --wait-selector body \
  https://example.com
```
For visual output, enable on-demand layout and write a viewport PNG, a full-document PNG, or a paginated PDF:
```bash
moli fetch --layout --dump screenshot https://example.com > page.png
moli fetch --layout --dump screenshot_full https://example.com > full-page.png
moli fetch --layout --dump pdf https://example.com > page.pdf
```
To export a page after an explicit interaction, combine `--eval` (or
`--eval-file`) with `--dump`. The expression runs after page readiness;
promises are awaited, and any pending navigation is followed before export.
Its return value is discarded without serialization. An exception fails the
command without emitting a dump.
```bash
moli fetch --eval 'document.querySelector("button.show-details").click()' \
  --dump markdown https://example.com
```
Only the supplied expression performs interactions. W

Pinky 
  Let AI use your iPhone or Android phone, with you in the loop: any agent from macOS, Windows or Linux, or Pinky itself, right on the phone.  
  Download  ·  Get started  ·  FAQ  ·  Discord  
 English ·  简体中文  ·  日本語  ·  Türkçe  
    A real Claude Code run on an Android 16 emulator. Pinky asks before payments by default; this run also asks before messages.  
Pinky lets any agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor or a script) operate a real iPhone or Android phone over MCP, while you watch on your computer, approve risky steps, take over and review what happened. Pinky can also do tasks by itself, with an AI model you choose: from your computer, or in Pinky's app right on the phone, with no computer at all. Whoever does the task, approvals are enforced by Pinky's gateway, not by instructions to the agent.
- **Every platform.** One app for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. It drives Android phones (Android 10 to 17) and iPhones on iOS 17.4 or later: nothing to install on iOS 27 and later, and Pinky on the iPhone, Pinky's app, installed once from a Mac with Xcode on iOS 17.4 to 26, which you can also choose on iOS 27 (tried there, on a phone below it and on Simulators; [details](#phones)).
- **Tiny and native.** The window is drawn by [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo) on the GPU, with no Electron and no webview: a 16–22 MB download that idles at about 70 MB of memory and 0% CPU on a Mac.
- **Any agent, one click.** Settings › Agents connects Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and more, and any agent that can use MCP servers works, on the same computer or over HTTP.
- **Pinky on the phone, no computer needed.** Pinky's app on Android and iPhone does tasks by itself with a model you choose, from DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi and GLM to Claude, GPT, Gemini and local models in Ollama or LM Studio. agentes.chat 
  The open-source, self-hosted Slack alternative where your team and AI agents work together.  
   Website  ·
   Cloud  ·
   Self-hosting  ·
   Features  ·
   Discussions 
Agents join your channels and DMs with a role, an owner and a budget, work where everyone can see,
and ask before anything sensitive. They think with Claude, ChatGPT and Codex, Gemini, Grok or any
OpenRouter model, use MCP tools, and get a computer and a browser of their own. Self-hosting is
free and always will be (AGPL-3.0, no license key), or use agentes.chat Cloud, the paid, hosted
option: both run this same codebase. Changing it without publishing your changes, or reselling it
under your own brand? There is a [commercial license](COMMERCIAL.md).
## Why agentes.chat
- **One conversation for people and agents.** Agents are members of the workspace, not a sidebar
  bot: they read the channel, answer when it's theirs to answer, and hand work back and forth.
- **Safe by default.** Merges, deploys and anything a connector marks sensitive wait for a person's
  approval in the chat. Every model call is budgeted and recorded per agent.
- **Agents that actually do the work.** Their own computer, a real browser you can watch and take
  over, Claude Code and Codex, routines on a schedule or an event, memory that learns.
- **Yours to run.** One command on a Linux server, Postgres as the only dependency, web, desktop and
  phone apps that connect to your server.
An open-source alternative to team chat with bolted-on AI bots, and to single-player agent apps such
as Grok Bot, ChatGPT dots, OpenBot.run and OpenMausBot (all of which it imports from).
## Quick start
- **Cloud:** sign up at [agentes.chat](https://agentes.chat).
- **Your own server** (Linux):
  ```sh
  curl -fsSL https://agentes.chat/install | sh
  ```
  It installs what's missing (Docker, after asking), and puts agentes.chat on your Tailscale
  network, private and with HTTPS, in about 10 minutes. [SELF_HOSTING.md](SELF_HOSTING.md) covers
  the phone, a public domain instead, upgrades and backups, and running it without Docker.
Each organization adds its own model key (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, Z.ai, MiniMax, Command Code or
OpenRouter) in the app.

| --- | --- | --- |

itens.descricao_en: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
itens.readme:
# TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
  Aaron J. Li 1 ,
  Weijia Xu 2 ,
  Chandan Singh 2 ,
  Zixiao Chen 3 ,
  Jeevana Priya Inala 2 ,
  Charlotte Siska 3 ,
  Acar Tamersoy 3 ,
  Bin Yu 1 ,
  Ion Stoica 1 ,
  Michel Galley 2 ,
  Jianfeng Gao 2 
   1 UC Berkeley    2 Microsoft Research    3 Microsoft Security
  Our measurement on SWE-Bench tasks:  18.4–30.9% lower mean cost  across five agent–model
  combinations, cheaper in  all 30  repository × combination cells, and Pass@1 up in
   4 of 5 .  Results 
TokenEconomizer makes coding agents cheaper to run in the repositories you work in often,
without changing the agent itself. It learns from the sessions an agent has already run in a
repository, and uses that experience to cut waste in the sessions that follow. It has three
mechanisms:
- **Micro-skills: remember how the repository works.** Sessions keep rediscovering the same
  facts: a build step that must run first, the spelling of a command that works here
  (`python -m pytest` where `pytest` is missing, `npx tsc` where `tsc` is), an environment
  variable a command needs, where generated files live. Micro-skills learns such facts, in any
  language, from two sources: failures that repeat across sessions, and a model that reviews the
  recent sessions every *k* sessions (*k* = 3) and proposes facts. A fact is stated at the start
  of each session once three sessions have confirmed it, and dropped when later sessions
  contradict it.
- **Tool pruning: stop loading tools that go unused.** Every loaded tool's definition is sent with
  every request. A tool that goes unused over *p* prompts spread across at least *m* sessions, or
  over *s* sessions of any length (*p* = 10, *m* = 2, *s* = 5), is left out of the next sessions
  through the agent's own settings. One command brings it back.
- **Failure-loop intervention (the loop guard): step in when a turn is stuck.** When a turn (the
  agent's work on one prompt) keeps hitting the same failures, a judge model checks whether it is
  stuck. If the judge is at least *c* sure (*c* = 0.7), the agent gets a redirect (a short note,
  added to its context, to try another approach), at most *r* times per turn (*r* = 1). If the
  turn is still stuck after that, TokenEconomizer tells you how to stop it; it never stops a turn
  itself.
TokenEconomizer is a plugin for **Claude Code**, **Codex**, the **GitHub Copilot CLI** and **Pi**,
with experimental support for **opencod

# DS Bot
English | [中文](README.zh.md)
DS Bot is an open-source project built on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), available as a standalone desktop app or as a DSH plugin. It turns DSH into bots that you create, talk to and work with.
## Sponsors
 ModelGo is a reliable, high-performance, enterprise-grade AI API aggregation platform. Access leading AI models—including Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, and DeepSeek—with a single API key. Sign up now and get 40% off DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Exclusive perks for DS-Bot users: get $0.50 in credits when you sign up, earn another $2 after your first API call, and receive up to $10 in bonus credits when you top up! Try it now:  ModelGo Official Website  
## Install
**Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux)**
The desktop app brings its own DSH, so you don't need to install DSH first. Download the installer for your system from [Releases](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot/releases/latest), open it, and set up a model in Settings (it can also copy your existing bot team from DSH).
If your system warns about an unsigned app: on Windows select **More info** → **Run anyway**; on macOS open **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security** and select **Open Anyway**.
**As a plugin in DSH**
First install DSH and set up at least one model in it. DS Bot uses the models from DSH.
- **DSH Desktop**: In the sidebar, select **Plugins** → **Add plugin**, enter `ds-bot` (in mainland China, set **Registry** to **Mainland China mirror**), then select **Install** and **Enable now**.
- **DSH Web** (needs Node.js `22.19` or later, and pnpm):
```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1 plugin --profile web add ds-bot
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.1 web
```
**Docker (NAS, Linux server)**
See [`docker/README.md`](docker/README.md).
## Setup
I strongly recommend that you set up your other bots and group chats by just talking to a bot.
### Web search
DS Bot selects its `auto` search provider for the whole profile. If you disable `web-search-auto`, also select another registered search provider in that profile. See [Web search](ds-bot/README.md#web-search) and the [recovery steps](docs/known-issues.md#web-search-fails-everywhere-after-turning-off-web-search-auto).
## Features
### Bot
You can do all your talking and work with one bot, in one window. You don't need to worry about the context behind it. The bot's details page shows its info, and there you can pick the model and thinking level you want it to use. You can switch model
